fields.html:
Assess your Neck Pain

Hey there! This assessment tool is designed by our experts. We will ask you a series of questions to better understand your symptoms. Based on a differential analysis of your responses, this tool will generate a preliminary diagnosis for you. This process should take about 5–10 minutes. Find a quiet corner, and let’s get started!

Please note that your information shared here is completely safe and is used only for arriving at the assessment results. The assessment results are indicative and do not substitute medical expert consultation in any way. Appropriate user discretion is advised. You may refer to our Terms of Service for further clarity.

fields.label: 1. Where is your neck pain located?

choices.value: Localized in one or more spots
choices.label: Localized in one or more spots

choices.value: Extends to one or both of the arms & hands
choices.label: Extends to one or both of the arms & hands

fields.html:
Did You Know?

"Tech neck" is a strain on the neck and spine caused by looking down at screens for long periods, leading to poor posture, pain, and stiffness.

fields.label: 2. Do you experience unbearable pain or stiffness in other joints of the body as well?

fields.html:
Did You Know?

Arthritis is a condition where the joints become swollen, painful, and stiff, making movement harder. It can happen for different reasons, with osteoarthritis (wear and tear arthritis) and rheumatoid arthritis (auto-immune arthritis) being the most common.

fields.label: 3. How would you describe your symptoms?

choices.value: Muscle stiffness (tightness, inability to move though full normal range of motion)
choices.label: Muscle stiffness (tightness, inability to move though full normal range of motion)

choices.value: Grinding or popping sensation when you turn your neck
choices.label: Grinding or popping sensation when you turn your neck

choices.value: Lack of neck control, shakiness, abnormal neck movements, difficulty in keeping the head up
choices.label: Lack of neck control, shakiness, abnormal neck movements, difficulty in keeping the head up

choices.value: Odd sensations such as pins & needles, numbness, tingling sensations along with pain
choices.label: Odd sensations such as pins & needles, numbness, tingling sensations along with pain

fields.html:
Did You Know?

The neck's intricate anatomy consists of seven cervical vertebrae, numerous muscles, and vital nerves, all working together to support head movement and protect the spinal cord.

fields.label: 4. Do you experience the following symptoms?

choices.value: Unusual weakness or lack of coordination in your arms or legs
choices.label: Unusual weakness or lack of coordination in your arms or legs

choices.value: Any loss of muscle tone or muscle size in your legs.
choices.label: Any loss of muscle tone or muscle size in your legs.

fields.html:
Did You Know?

Nerve pinching in the neck, often caused by a herniated disc or arthritis, can lead to sharp pain, tingling, or numbness that radiates down the arm due to pressure on the spinal nerves.

fields.label: 5. Pain on a scale - 1 being the least amount of pain and 10 being the highest (Options to presented as a visual scale)

choices.label: 1 - Mild - Pain is very mild, barely noticeable
2 - Minor - Annoying and may have occasional sudden bouts of the localized pain
3 - Uncomfortable - Pain is noticeable and distracting but bearable
4 - Moderate - Distracting when not involved in an activity
5 - Distracting - Moderately strong pain, that cannot be ignored for more than a few minutes
6 - Distressing - Moderately strong pain that interferes with daily activities
7 - Severe - Pain that limits your ability to perform daily activity
8 - Intense - Physical activity is severely limited
9 - Excruciating - Unable to converse. Crying out uncontrollably

fields.html:
Did You Know?

The neck has an impressive range of motion, allowing up to 180 degrees of rotation, thanks to the unique structure of the cervical spine, which includes flexible vertebrae and specialized joints.

fields.label: 6. Is your neck pain accompanied by, or did it start after, any of the following?

choices.value: Injury from falls, trauma, accidents, or sports activities
choices.label: Injury from falls, trauma, accidents, or sports activities

choices.value: Any autoimmune disorder such as Rheumatoid arthritis, Multiple sclerosis
choices.label: Any autoimmune disorder such as Rheumatoid arthritis, Multiple sclerosis

choices.value: Known Spinal deformities (uneven shoulders/hips/waist; hunchback; or an unusual forward curve in neck or lower back)
choices.label: Known Spinal deformities (uneven shoulders/hips/waist; hunchback; or an unusual forward curve in neck or lower back)

fields.html:
Did You Know?

Neck pain can sometimes cause chest pain if nerves in the cervical spine are compressed, triggering referred pain that mimics heart-related issues.

fields.label: 7. Which activities seem to trigger or worsen your pain?

choices.value: Turning your neck to the left or right
choices.label: Turning your neck to the left or right

fields.html:
Did You Know?

Neck pain that worsens when bending sideways can be caused by facet joint dysfunction, where the small joints in the spine become irritated or inflamed, making movement painful.

fields.label: Muscle Lower Back
fields.default: Your symptoms are most likely due to the Muscular Imbalance arising due to the deconditioning of your neck muscles because of years of wear and tear and neglect. To keep your neck functioning optimally, it's essential to balance muscle length and strength between opposing muscle groups. As you age, the muscles, tendons, and ligaments become thicker and less flexible, increasing the risk of injury. With a proper self-care routine, you can prevent further damage and reverse some of the damage already done. The betterhoodTM routine focuses on targeted muscle strengthening and postural correction to alleviate cervical misalignment, reduce excessive loading, and enhance bone density and tissue recovery.

fields.label: Nerve Lower Back
fields.default: Your symptoms are most likely due to the Compressed Nerves due to various underlying muskuloskeletal issues. Your spine is the key pathway for your spinal cord, linking your brain to nerves in your arms, legs, and trunk. With 31 pairs of nerves branching from the spinal cord, any compression or damage can lead to pain. This often results from wear and tear on cervical bones, joints, or disks. With a proper self-care routine, you can prevent further damage and reverse some of the damage already done. The betterhoodTM routine focuses on targeted muscle strengthening and postural correction to alleviate cervical misalignment, reduce excessive loading, and enhance bone density and tissue recovery.

fields.label: Bone Lower Back
fields.default: Your symptoms are most likely due to the Cervical Instability arising due to the poor bone health. As you age, bone density decreases (osteoporosis), making bones more prone to fractures. Cervical fractures can cause instability, leading to painful vertebra slippage. Additionally, aging causes your cervical disks to flatten or break down, worsening cervical instability. With a proper self-care routine, you can prevent further damage and reverse some of the damage already done. The betterhoodTM routine focuses on targeted muscle strengthening and postural correction to alleviate cervical misalignment, reduce excessive loading, and enhance bone density and tissue recovery.

fields.label: Joint Lower Back
fields.default: Your symptoms are most likely due to the excessive wear and tear of cervical joints. Your spine consists of 33 different bones connected by spinal joints. As you age, excessive strain on cervical joints from improper posture or weak muscles wear down the protective tissues, leading to osteoarthritis and pain. The bony outgrowths that form as a result can further increase the pain. With a proper self-care routine, you can prevent further damage and reverse some of the damage already done. The betterhoodTM routine focuses on targeted muscle strengthening and postural correction to alleviate cervical misalignment, reduce excessive loading, and enhance bone density and tissue recovery.
